Paid plans: POST /platform/app-sms/number with {app, company_name, business_type, website, address1, city, state, zip_code, contact_first, contact_last, support_email, support_phone} - the platform leases a toll-free number (~$2/mo), renders the app-branded opt-in evidence, submits the carrier registration, and polls status. Once approved, the broker automatically originates that app's SMS from its own number.
Status: `benmore sms <app>` shows dedicated_status (pending_carrier | active | denied).

Removing a dedicated number (DELETE /platform/app-sms/number) releases it at the provider. A release that fails is queued for retry, so a removed number does not stay leased; when the retry cannot be recorded the request answers 502 and the number stays on the app.

A carrier verdict applies only to the registration it was issued for, and only while that number is still pending_carrier: after removing a number and requesting a new one, the old registration's verdict cannot mark the new, unapproved number active or denied. Transitions: pending_carrier -> active (carrier status COMPLETE), pending_carrier -> denied (DENIED, CLOSED, REQUIRES_UPDATES; `dedicated_status_detail` names which); both are final for that number.

POST /platform/app-sms/number answers 409 when the app already has a dedicated number or a request in progress, so a double submit leases one number. A request that fails part-way releases the number it leased (a failed release is queued for retry) and leaves nothing behind. A request in progress shows in GET /platform/app-sms as `dedicated_status: pending_carrier`, with `dedicated_in_progress: true` and an empty `dedicated_number` until a number is leased; nothing is sent from the number before it is active, and Remove clears the request. A request left unfinished for over 30 minutes is cleared automatically and its number released.
